title: Guardian decode arbiter: routing policy, acceptance telemetry, and graceful fallback plan
creator: Avery Chen
description: Purpose: Design and implement a lightweight 'guardian' arbiter that makes per-request choices between a low-latency speculative decode path and the conservative baseline path. The guardian should: 1) use kernel and attention-capability signals to prefer fast-path kernels when safe, 2) compute an online acceptance score for speculative outputs so we can confidently commit or fall back before wasted compute accumulates, and 3) provide a deterministic, auditable fallback sequence that keeps latency SLOs while bounding cost regressions. Scope: runtime decision logic, telemetry surface, routing policy config, fallback executor, and rollout plan. Out of scope: model training changes, core kernel implementations (we assume kernel capability matrix is provided by infra), scheduler-level batch reshaping (handled in separate ticket). Goals: reduce median token-latency by targeted percentiles for interactive loads while keeping the 99th percentile regressions < 5% and controlling token cost delta to < 6% at rollout. Acceptance criteria are below.
acceptance_criteria: Guardian can route requests to speculative path and record an acceptance score within 2 ms overhead
End-to-end median token latency improvement >= 10% on our interactive bench for eligible workloads
99th percentile tail latency does not increase by more than 5% across the benchmark suite
Rollbackable configuration: disable speculative routing via feature flag with immediate effect
Telemetry exposes per-model acceptance histogram, per-kernel success rate, and resettable counters for failed fallbacks
Automated canary verifies that cost-per-token increase stays within configured threshold (default 6%) or aborts rollout
implementation_notes: Routing inputs: model_id, model_variant, seq_len, prefix_kv_hit_rate (from cache), kernel_fingerprint, device_affinity, tenant_tier

Acceptance signal design: lightweight classifier that compares fast-path top-k logits against baseline probe logits for a small prefill window; uses configurable confidence threshold and decay to avoid oscillation

Kernel capability table is read-only map provided by infra (format: kernel_fingerprint -> capabilities). Guardian consults this table to avoid using kernels without attention-optimization support for the request shape

Fallback semantics: on rejection or timeout, spawn a fallback decode on the baseline path with fast cancellation of speculative work if hardware supports preemption; otherwise record telemetry and accept increased token cost for that request
Backpressure: guardian must not block scheduler batching; decisions occur at pre-scheduling checkpoint (<1ms target) and are marked on request token header for downstream runtime executors
Config surface: per-route feature-flag, per-model acceptance_threshold, cost_safety_margin, fastpath_allowed_devices, and debug logging level
Rollout plan: start with internal canary on dev tenants (5% traffic), then beta customers (20%), monitor acceptance rate and cost delta, proceed to 100% if stable
Telemetry: expose time-series for acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, cost_delta, median/99th token latency by route and kernel. Add alert rules when fallback_rate > 10% or cost_delta > configured margin

Testing: unit tests for routing decisions, integration test with runtime stub that simulates kernel failures and delayed speculative acceptance. Add a comparison harness that computes quality regression (BLEU/EMB) on a labeled prompt set
Docs: add runtime configuration guide for operator and a short primer for PM/SEs explaining trade-offs and toggles
design_decisions: Prefer deterministic, rule-first approach: simple gating rules (kernel support, seq thresholds, cache hits) + small ML acceptance classifier for edge cases. Rationale: reduces surprise surface and aids debugging.
Keep acceptance classifier shallow and interpretable (logit-space deltas, token-level entropy heuristics) to minimize compute and to make decisions auditable.
Do not attempt aggressive speculative roll-forward for long sequences in first rollout. Limit speculative path to dialogs/prompt lengths < 1024 tokens and prefill sizes < 512 to control risk.
Fallback executor should be a prioritized baseline path; resource reservation for fallback slots (soft guarantee) to avoid cascading failures under load.
Telemetry-centric rollout: prioritize observable metrics over early optimistic thresholds; if acceptance distribution drifts we will tighten thresholds before expanding traffic.
Safety-first feature flag: default is disabled for enterprise customers with strict cost/SLA guarantees; enabled on hosted tier by default under canary control.
Audit trail: every decision must be logged with request_id, chosen_path, acceptance_score, kernel_fingerprint, and reason_code (rule|classifier|cache)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Speculative path could increase token cost if acceptance is low. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, cost_safety_margin config, and automated canary abort on cost spike.
Risk: Kernel mismatch leads to silent correctness regressions. Mitigation: require explicit kernel capability flag for attention optimizations and conservative gating when unknown.

Risk: Increased complexity in scheduler interactions. Mitigation: keep guardian decision upstream of batching and avoid changing batch shapes; work with scheduler team for telemetry integration and do a staged contract change.
Risk: Observability blind spots for rare failure modes. Mitigation: add sampled request traces (1/1000) containing logits, token hashes, and acceptance decisions to reproduce edge cases.
Risk: Rollout rollback lag. Mitigation: implement an emergency kill switch at the control plane that disables speculative routing cluster-wide within <30s
